payload.title: Rohan's team wins the animal quiz
decoys: They got a round of claps

payload.passage: At the zoo, Anaya found a long line of busy ants behind glass. The little ants carried leaves much bigger than themselves. A board said they were building a home under the ground. Anaya was amazed at how the tiny ants worked together.
payload.title: Busy Ants at the Zoo Display

payload.passage: Akash was a small boy but very quick on his feet. The bigger boys could not catch him on the field. He dribbled the ball past three players with ease. Then he passed it to his friend who scored.
payload.title: Akash dribbles past the bigger boys
decoys: He passed the ball to his friend
Speed helps a lot in football

payload.passage: A magician put on a show at the fair. He pulled a rabbit out of an empty hat and made coins disappear. The children gasped and could not guess how he did it. Diya thought the magician was the cleverest man at the fair.
payload.title: The Magician's Show at the Fair
decoys: He pulled a rabbit from a hat.

payload.passage: Roshan won a big bar of chocolate in a school quiz. There were six friends standing around him. Instead of eating it alone, he broke it into six pieces. Everyone got a share and cheered for Roshan.
payload.title: Roshan shares his prize chocolate
decoys: Roshan won the chocolate in a quiz
He broke it into six pieces
Winning is more fun with friends

payload.passage: A volleyball match was played in the bright sunshine. The ball flew high over the net many times. Salim gave a strong jump and hit a winning shot. His team scored and won the close match.
payload.title: Salim's jump shot wins volleyball
decoys: The ball flew over the net
His team won the close match

payload.passage: Rohan enjoys carving simple stamps from an old rubber. He cuts a star, a heart, and a little tree. He dips them in ink and stamps his books. Rohan likes to mark all his things with his own stamps.
payload.title: Rohan Carves Rubber Stamps
decoys: He cuts a star and a tree.

payload.passage: The museum had a corner about how letters were sent before. Meera saw old post boxes, stamps, and ink pens. A board explained that letters once took many days to reach. Meera was glad messages now travel so fast.
payload.title: How Letters Were Sent Long Ago

payload.passage: Ananya tried the ring toss game at the fair. She had to throw rings onto rows of bottles. On her last try, a ring landed neatly around a bottle. The man at the stall handed her a small teddy as a prize.
payload.title: Ananya Wins at the Ring Toss

payload.passage: A little girl's shoelace came undone on the busy stairs. She could nearly trip on the loose lace. Her elder brother bent down and tied it tight. They walked down the stairs safely.
payload.title: A brother ties the loose lace

payload.passage: A girl could not understand the new word in her story book. She frowned and felt like giving up. Her friend looked it up and explained the meaning. Now the girl enjoyed reading her book again.
payload.title: A friend helps with a hard new word
decoys: Helping a friend read is kind

payload.passage: The old well in the village had become dirty and unsafe. People could not draw clean water from it. The villagers cleaned it together over the weekend. Now they get fresh water from the well again.
payload.title: Villagers clean the dirty well together
decoys: People could not draw clean water
They cleaned it over the weekend
Working together helps the whole village

payload.passage: A baby sparrow sat trapped behind the window grill. It chirped and could not get out. Sahana opened the window slowly and gently. The little bird flew out into the open sky.
payload.title: Sahana frees the trapped sparrow
decoys: Freeing birds is a kind act

payload.passage: The food stalls at the fair smelled delicious. There were puffed rice, roasted corn, and sweet candy floss. Ravi chose the pink candy floss that melted on his tongue. He thought fair food always tasted the best.
payload.title: Tasty Treats at the Fair

payload.passage: Vikram watched a man make sugar shapes at the fair. The man poured hot melted sugar onto a cold plate. It set quickly into a shape of a bird. Vikram bought the sugar bird and ate it slowly.
payload.title: The Sugar Shape Maker at the Fair

payload.passage: Aditya likes to grow a small water plant in a jar. He placed a green sprig in clean water on the sill. New roots and leaves slowly grew over the weeks. Aditya was happy to watch his jar plant thrive.
payload.title: Aditya Grows a Plant in a Jar
decoys: He placed a green sprig in water.

payload.passage: Anjali likes to make friendship bands from coloured thread. She ties and twists the strands into pretty patterns. She gives the bands to her friends as little gifts. Anjali's friends always smile when they get a new band.
payload.title: Anjali Makes Friendship Bands

payload.passage: Meera and her brother got lost in the maze at the fair. Tall green walls turned this way and that. They took many wrong turns and giggled each time. At last they found the way out and cheered together.
payload.title: Finding the Way Out of the Maze
decoys: The walls were tall and green.

payload.passage: Pari forgot her lines during the school play and froze. The crowd grew quiet and she felt like crying. From the side, her friend softly reminded her of the words. Pari remembered, finished the play, and got a big clap.
payload.title: A friend helps Pari remember her lines
decoys: She got a big clap at the end

payload.passage: Two friends played a long game of ludo on Sunday. The dice kept giving small numbers to Sahil. But near the end, he rolled a six three times. He moved all his pieces home and won the game.
payload.title: Sahil wins the long ludo game

payload.passage: Anjali enjoys making her own bird feeder. She fills an old cup with seeds and hangs it up. She waits quietly by the window to watch. Anjali smiles when little birds come to eat her seeds.
payload.title: Anjali Makes a Bird Feeder
decoys: She fills a cup with seeds.

payload.passage: Heavy rain flooded a poor family's small house. Their books and clothes got wet and ruined. The neighbours collected dry clothes and food to give them. The family felt grateful for the warm help.
payload.title: Neighbours help a flooded family
decoys: Neighbours support each other in trouble

payload.passage: Hari kept losing the marble game to the older boys. He watched how they aimed and flicked their marbles. Then he practised his aim alone for many days. The next time, Hari won most of the marbles.
payload.title: Hari improves his marble game

payload.passage: Riya and her cousins played beach volleyball on the sand. They patted the ball back and forth over a low net. The soft sand made it tricky to jump. Everyone got hot and happy in the bright sun.
payload.title: Playing Volleyball on the Beach

payload.passage: The museum had a special part you could touch. Rohan ran his fingers over rough rocks and smooth shells. He felt the soft fur of an old rug. This hands-on room was Rohan's favourite of the whole museum.
payload.title: The Touch Room at the Museum

payload.passage: Two brothers played table tennis in the garage every evening. At first the younger brother always lost. He kept practising his serve and his quick returns. Soon he could beat his elder brother sometimes.
payload.title: A boy improves at table tennis

payload.passage: A baby bird fell from its nest in the tall mango tree. It chirped weakly on the hard ground. Harsh climbed up carefully and placed it back in the nest. The mother bird returned and fed it again.
payload.title: Harsh returns the baby bird to its nest
decoys: The baby bird fell to the ground
The mother bird returned to feed it

payload.passage: Riya loves to make her own puppets from wooden spoons. She paints a face on the back of each spoon. She glues on woollen hair and a cloth dress. Riya's spoon puppets star in her little plays.
payload.title: Riya Makes Wooden Spoon Puppets
decoys: She paints a face on the spoon.

payload.passage: The puppy near the school had a thorn stuck in its paw. It limped and whined in pain. A gentle girl pulled out the thorn with care. The puppy licked her hand and walked happily.
payload.title: A girl removes the puppy's thorn

payload.passage: The class had a memory game during the rainy break. Cards were placed face down on the desk. Ritu remembered where each card was hidden. She matched the most pairs and won the game.
payload.title: Ritu wins the memory card game
decoys: A good memory helps in games

payload.passage: Ishaan likes to grow seeds in little cups. He pushed bean seeds into the wet soil and waited. After a few days, tiny green shoots poked out. Ishaan was thrilled to watch his little plants grow taller each day.
payload.title: Ishaan Grows Seeds in Cups

payload.passage: A girls' kabaddi match was played at the school meet. The two teams were equal till the last raid. Nita took a deep breath and made a clever raid. She tagged two girls and won the match for her team.
payload.title: Nita's clever raid wins the match
decoys: A smart raid can win kabaddi

payload.passage: Aditya likes to grow a small herb pot on the window. He planted coriander and watered it every day. Soon green leaves filled the little pot. Aditya was happy when his mother used his herbs in cooking.
payload.title: Aditya Grows a Herb Pot

payload.passage: Kabir has started learning to play the drums. He taps out a steady beat with two sticks. At first his rhythm was slow and wobbly. Now Kabir can keep a beat along with his favourite songs.
payload.title: Kabir Learns to Play Drums
decoys: His beat was wobbly at first.

payload.passage: Faisal's team was losing the football match by two goals. The players felt tired and almost gave up. But Faisal told them to keep trying till the end. They scored three goals quickly and won the match.
payload.title: Faisal's team never gives up and wins
decoys: The team was losing by two goals
Hope can change a losing game

payload.passage: Two teams played a relay with water in spoons. They had to carry water without spilling it. Sonal's team moved carefully and lost the least water. They filled their bottle first and won the game.
payload.title: Sonal's team wins the water relay

payload.passage: Diya visited a museum room about old kings and queens. Their thrones, crowns, and robes were on display. A guide told the story of one brave queen. Diya listened closely and learned about a time long ago.
payload.title: Kings and Queens at the Museum

payload.passage: Sara loves to make snow globes from old jars. She glues a small toy to the inside of the lid. She fills the jar with water and tiny glitter. When Sara shakes it, the glitter swirls like snow.
payload.title: Sara Makes a Snow Globe
decoys: She glues a toy to the lid.

payload.passage: The fair had a stall where you could win goldfish. Children threw small balls into little bowls of water. If a ball landed in a bowl, they won a fish. Aarav tried hard but his ball missed every time.
payload.title: The Goldfish Game at the Fair

payload.passage: A boy named Chetan loved kite flying more than any game. His kite kept diving down because of weak knots. His uncle taught him to tie strong, neat knots. Soon his kite flew high and steady.
payload.title: Chetan learns to fly his kite steadily
decoys: Good knots help the kite fly

payload.passage: On sports day, a boy from another class hurt his ankle and could not walk. Mohan offered his shoulder for support at once. He helped the boy reach the shaded tent for rest. The teachers thanked Mohan for his quick kindness.
payload.title: Mohan helps an injured boy on sports day
decoys: The boy hurt his ankle badly
He helped him reach the shaded tent
Kindness should be shown to everyone

payload.passage: The boys played gilli danda in the open field. Sameer hit the small stick high into the air. It flew the longest distance of the whole game. His team scored the most points and cheered.
payload.title: Sameer's long hit wins the gilli danda game
decoys: Old games are still good fun

payload.passage: An old man's umbrella turned inside out in the strong wind. He struggled to fix it in the heavy rain. Two children ran out and helped him hold it straight. They walked him to the shop under their own umbrella.
payload.title: Children help an old man in the storm
decoys: They walked him to the shop
Helping in bad weather is kind

payload.passage: Meera ran along the beach flying a long ribbon in the wind. The bright ribbon trailed and twisted behind her. She made big loops in the air as she ran. Meera felt as free as the birds in the sky.
payload.title: Running with a Ribbon on the Beach

payload.passage: Aarav and his sister searched the beach for crabs at low tide. They lifted stones and peeked into wet holes. They spotted three tiny crabs scuttling away. Aarav was careful not to harm the little creatures.
payload.title: Searching for Crabs at the Beach

payload.passage: Ravi found a message in a bottle on the beach. He pulled out a small note rolled up inside. The note had a smiley face and a kind hello. Ravi wondered who had sent it across the wide sea.
payload.title: Ravi Finds a Bottle Message
decoys: The note had a smiley face.
He pulled out a small note.

payload.passage: Riya loves to write little stories in her notebook. She thinks of brave heroes and faraway lands. She draws a small picture at the top of each story. Riya dreams of making a whole book one day.
payload.title: Riya Writes Her Own Stories
decoys: She draws a picture for each.

payload.passage: Diya saw stuffed animals from many lands at the museum. There was a lion, a bear, and a big spotted leopard. They stood so still that they looked almost alive. A board told her where each animal once lived.
payload.title: Animals Display at the Museum

payload.passage: An old farmer's bullock cart got stuck in the soft mud. The wheels would not move forward at all. Some village boys pushed hard from behind. The cart came free and rolled on smoothly.
payload.title: Boys free the stuck bullock cart

payload.passage: Priya saw the polar bear in its cool, white home. The huge bear had thick fur to keep it warm. It dived into the water and swam with strong paws. Priya learned that polar bears live where it is snowy and cold.
payload.title: The Polar Bear at the Zoo

payload.passage: Tara and her brother bargained at the bag stall. The seller asked for a high price for a school bag. Their mother spoke politely and asked for less. After some talk, they agreed on a fair price and bought the bag.
payload.title: Bargaining for a School Bag
decoys: The seller asked a high price.

payload.passage: During the school fair, a small boy lost his money for a ride. He stood near the merry-go-round looking sad. A girl shared half of her own ride tokens. The two went on the ride together happily.
payload.title: A girl shares ride tokens at the fair

payload.passage: A boy in the playground fell and his nose started to bleed. He was scared at the sight of the blood. His friend stayed calm and pressed a clean tissue gently. He walked the boy to the school nurse.
payload.title: A boy helps his bleeding friend
decoys: He walked him to the nurse

payload.passage: Priya found a face-painting stall at the fair. The artist painted bright flowers on each child's cheek. Priya chose a yellow butterfly and a tiny star. She looked in the mirror and loved her painted face.
payload.title: Getting Her Face Painted

payload.passage: An old lady could not lift the heavy shutter of her shop. It was stuck and very stiff in the morning. Two boys came and pulled it up together. She opened her shop on time and thanked them.
payload.title: Boys lift the stuck shop shutter
decoys: She opened her shop on time

payload.passage: A girl named Komal was scared to climb the rope in gym. Her hands felt weak and she would slip down. She practised gripping the rope every day. Soon she climbed right to the top and rang the bell.
payload.title: Komal climbs the gym rope to the top
decoys: She rang the bell at top

payload.passage: Kabir and his cousins played beach cricket on the sand. They used a flat piece of wood as a bat. The soft sand made it hard to run quickly. Everyone laughed and cheered until the game finally ended.
payload.title: Playing Cricket on the Beach
decoys: They used wood as a bat.

payload.passage: A water pipe burst and flooded the lane with muddy water. People could not walk to the market. Some neighbours brought brooms and pushed the water into the drain. By evening the lane was dry and clean again.
payload.title: Neighbours clear the flooded lane together
decoys: A water pipe burst in the lane
They pushed the water into the drain

payload.passage: Sara joined the sack race at the fair. The children climbed into big cloth sacks and hopped to the finish. Many of them tumbled over halfway through. Sara hopped fast and came in third, all out of breath.
payload.title: The Sack Race at the Fair

payload.passage: Pinky could swim well but her little brother could not. He slipped and started to splash in the shallow end. Pinky reached him quickly and pulled him to safety. Their mother thanked Pinky for being so quick.
payload.title: Pinky saves her little brother in the pool
decoys: Knowing to swim keeps us safe

payload.passage: Diya likes to weave little mats from coloured paper strips. She lays some strips down and threads others across. The strips lock together into a neat pattern. Diya uses her paper mats under her small flower pots.
payload.title: Diya Weaves Paper Mats

payload.passage: The class played a quiz on famous sports during games period. They answered questions about players and games. Yogesh knew the most answers correctly. His team won the sports quiz happily.
payload.title: Yogesh's team wins the sports quiz

payload.passage: Heavy bags of grain had to be moved into the storeroom. The shopkeeper was old and could not lift them. A few strong boys offered to carry the bags inside. They finished the work and the shopkeeper was grateful.
payload.title: Boys help the shopkeeper move grain bags
decoys: Helping elders is a noble deed

payload.passage: An old man's letter slipped from his hand into a puddle. The ink began to run on the wet paper. A boy carefully picked it up and dried it gently. He helped the old man read the smudged words.
payload.title: A boy saves an old man's wet letter
decoys: The letter fell in a puddle

payload.passage: At the zoo pond, many turtles sat on a flat rock. They moved very slowly and pulled their heads into their shells. When a leaf fell into the water, one turtle swam after it. Diya could have watched the slow turtles all day.
payload.title: Slow Turtles at the Zoo Pond
decoys: The turtles sat on a rock.
A leaf fell into the water.

payload.passage: Vikram likes to build tall towers with playing cards. He leans two cards together to make each level. The tower wobbles if he moves too fast. Vikram once built a tower five whole levels high.
payload.title: Vikram Builds Card Towers
decoys: It wobbles if he is fast.

payload.passage: Ravi has taken up the hobby of growing plants. He has small pots of mint, money plant, and a tiny rose. Every morning he waters them and checks for new leaves. Ravi feels happy each time a fresh bud appears.
payload.title: Ravi's Hobby of Growing Plants
decoys: He has a pot of mint.

payload.passage: Priya visited a museum about old machines. She saw the first telephones, radios, and big cameras. A guide showed how a hand-crank machine once worked. Priya could not believe people used such heavy things before.
payload.title: Old Machines at the Museum
decoys: A guide turned a hand crank.

payload.passage: Kabaddi needs both strength and quick breathing. Vimal took a deep breath and ran into the other team. He touched two players and rushed back to his side. His team got two points and cheered for him.
payload.title: Vimal scores two points in kabaddi

payload.passage: A small boy could not open his tight bottle cap. He tried hard but his hands were too weak. His friend Imtiaz twisted the cap open for him. The boy drank his water and said thank you.
payload.title: Imtiaz opens a tight bottle for a friend

payload.passage: Anaya loves to knit with soft wool. Her grandmother taught her how to hold the needles. She is slowly making a small scarf for her doll. Anaya feels proud each time the scarf grows a little longer.
payload.title: Anaya Knits a Doll's Scarf

payload.passage: Veer enjoys building bridges across a stream of water. He lays flat stones one after another. He tests if they hold his weight before he steps. Veer is proud when he crosses on his own stone bridge.
payload.title: Veer Builds a Stone Bridge

payload.passage: The library books were piled in a great mess on the floor. The librarian looked tired and overwhelmed. A group of students offered to sort them by number. Soon every book sat neatly on its shelf.
payload.title: Students help the tired librarian sort books
decoys: The books were in a mess

payload.passage: Diya enjoys making greeting cards by hand. She folds the paper, draws a picture, and writes kind words inside. She made a bright card for her mother's birthday. Diya thinks handmade cards are more special than bought ones.
payload.title: Diya Makes Handmade Cards
decoys: She made one for her mother.

payload.passage: Meera enjoys making her own paper fans. She folds a sheet back and forth like an accordion. She glues one end together so it opens out. Meera waves her bright paper fan on hot afternoons.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Fans
decoys: She folds the paper back and forth.
She waves it on hot days.

payload.passage: The whole class went to play in the big school field. They split into two teams for a relay game. Each child cheered loudly for their own team. In the end, both teams said it was great fun.
payload.title: The class enjoys a relay game together

payload.passage: The zoo had a small section for night animals kept in the dark. Karan saw bats hanging upside down from a branch. A red light let him watch without bothering them. Karan learned that bats use sound to find their way at night.
payload.title: Bats in the Zoo's Dark Room

payload.passage: Mukesh won the running race by a long way. But he saw a younger boy fall down near the finish. Instead of cheering, he went back to help the boy up. The crowd clapped for Mukesh's kind heart.
payload.title: Mukesh shows kindness after winning
decoys: Mukesh won by a long way

payload.passage: Roopa saw her teacher carrying a heavy pile of notebooks. The pile wobbled and almost fell from her hands. Roopa ran up and took half the notebooks at once. She carried them all the way to the staff room.
payload.title: Roopa helps her teacher carry notebooks
decoys: She carried them to the staff room
Helping teachers is a kind act

payload.passage: The school had a wheelbarrow race on its sports day. One child walked on hands while another held the legs. Bittu and his partner moved fast and stayed steady. They reached the line first and won.
payload.title: Bittu's pair wins the wheelbarrow race

payload.passage: A poor boy near the park had no slippers to wear. His feet were getting hurt on the hot road. Chetan asked his mother and gave the boy his old slippers. The boy wore them and walked away happily.
payload.title: Chetan gives slippers to a poor boy
decoys: He gave away his old slippers

payload.passage: Sara loves to fold paper into animals. This art is called origami, her teacher said. She has made cranes, frogs, and a little fox. Sara keeps her paper animals lined up on the windowsill.
payload.title: Sara's Hobby of Paper Folding
decoys: She has made a paper fox.

payload.passage: Jatin felt very homesick on his first day at a new school. He missed his old friends and would not smile. His new teacher gave him a small task to feel useful. Slowly Jatin cheered up and made some new friends.
payload.title: A teacher helps Jatin feel at home
decoys: The teacher gave him a small task
New places can be scary at first

payload.passage: A new student could not find the right classroom on her first day. She wandered the long corridor looking lost. Aastha noticed her and asked which class she needed. Then she walked the girl right to her room.
payload.title: Aastha guides a lost new student
decoys: She walked her to the room

payload.passage: The fair had a small train that went around the ground. Little children sat inside the colourful carriages. The train tooted its horn at every turn. Vikram and his baby sister rode it together twice.
payload.title: The Little Train at the Fair

payload.passage: Tara stopped at the fish tank in the zoo. Bright fish of every colour swam past the glass. A small striped fish hid inside a soft sea plant. Tara pressed her nose to the glass and watched them glide by.
payload.title: Bright Fish in the Zoo Tank
decoys: A striped fish hid in a plant.
Tara pressed her nose to the glass.

payload.passage: Rohan tried the strength game at the fair. He had to swing a big hammer to ring a high bell. He hit the pad hard, but the bell barely moved. Rohan laughed and said he would grow stronger and try again.
payload.title: The Strength Game at the Fair

payload.passage: Sara enjoys making her own simple puzzles. She draws a picture and sticks it onto card. Then she cuts it into many odd pieces. Sara mixes them up and asks her friends to put it back.
payload.title: Sara Makes Her Own Puzzles
decoys: She sticks the picture on card.

payload.passage: Vikram likes to solve jigsaw puzzles on holidays. He spreads the pieces out and finds the corners first. Slowly the picture comes together, piece by piece. Vikram feels great joy when the last piece fits in place.
payload.title: Vikram's Hobby of Solving Puzzles

payload.passage: Tara enjoys pressing leaves to make pictures. She dips a leaf in paint and presses it on paper. The leaf leaves a perfect print with all its lines. Tara filled a page with leaf prints of many shapes.
payload.title: Tara Makes Leaf Prints
decoys: She dips a leaf in paint.
The print shows all the lines.

payload.passage: Rahul loves to play cricket in the park every evening. He practises his batting against the old brick wall. Slowly his shots became stronger and straighter. Now he is one of the best batsmen in his team.
payload.title: Rahul practises hard to bat well
decoys: Rahul practises against a brick wall

payload.passage: The sweeper aunty had hurt her hand and could not work. The school ground was full of dry leaves. The children picked up brooms and swept the ground for her. The aunty thanked them and rested her hand.
payload.title: Children sweep the ground for the aunty
decoys: The aunty had hurt her hand

payload.passage: In the game of tag, one child must chase and touch others. Farhan was very quick and hard to catch. He dodged left and right and ran in circles. No one could tag him for the whole game.
payload.title: Farhan is too quick to be tagged

payload.passage: The classroom plant on the window was drooping and dry. The other children walked past it every day. But Aditya remembered to bring a small jug of water. He watered the plant gently, and soon its leaves stood up green.
payload.title: Aditya cares for the classroom plant
decoys: The plant was drooping and dry
He brought a small jug of water
Plants need water to stay alive

payload.passage: Megha tripped and fell during the long race on sports day. Her knee hurt and the others ran ahead. But she got up and kept running till the end. The crowd clapped loudly for her brave finish.
payload.title: Megha finishes the race after falling

payload.passage: During the match, Varun dropped an easy catch at first. His teammates looked a little upset. But Varun did not give up and stayed alert. In the next over, he took a brilliant flying catch.
payload.title: Varun makes up for his dropped catch
decoys: Never give up after a mistake

payload.passage: Two friends played a clapping memory game in the bus. Each added a clap pattern to repeat. Harini remembered the whole long pattern. She did not slip and won the game.
payload.title: Harini wins the clapping memory game
decoys: A good memory wins the game

payload.passage: Priya's father was washing the family car on Sunday. Priya wanted to help, so she held the bucket and passed the cloth. She also wiped the shiny wheels with great care. By lunchtime the car looked brand new and clean.
payload.title: Priya helps wash the family car

payload.passage: Anaya and her grandmother bought fresh fish at the market. The seller cleaned and cut the fish for them. He wrapped it neatly in paper for the trip home. Anaya held her nose the whole time but did not complain.
payload.title: Buying Fish with Grandmother

payload.passage: Meera visited the small zoo pond full of pink flamingos. The tall birds stood on one thin leg in the shallow water. They dipped their curved beaks to find food. Meera wondered how they balanced so well on just one leg.
payload.title: Flamingos at the Zoo Pond

payload.passage: A boy on the train could not lift his bag to the top rack. It was too heavy for his small arms. A kind uncle near him lifted it up easily. The boy thanked the uncle with a happy smile.
payload.title: An uncle helps a boy lift his bag
decoys: The boy gave a happy smile

payload.passage: The fishermen pulled their boats onto the beach in the morning. Their nets were full of silver fish from the sea. People gathered to buy the fresh catch right there. Priya watched the busy work from the soft sand.
payload.title: Fishermen Bring Their Catch
decoys: The nets were full of fish.

payload.passage: Naresh wanted to bowl spin like the players on TV. His first tries spun the wrong way. He practised with a tennis ball every evening. Soon his spin turned sharply and fooled the batsmen.
payload.title: Naresh learns to bowl spin

payload.passage: Veer likes to make musical shakers from old tins. He fills each tin with rice, beans, or seeds. Each one makes a different rattling sound. Veer shakes them in time with the music he loves.
payload.title: Veer Makes Musical Shakers

payload.passage: When Rohan's mother had a bad headache, he kept the house very quiet. He switched off the loud television and drew the curtains. He brought her a glass of water and a soft pillow. His mother rested well and felt much better by evening.
payload.title: Rohan helps his sick mother rest
decoys: Rohan switched off the loud television
He brought a glass of water
Children must care for sick people

payload.passage: Two boys played a coin flicking game on the table. They had to flick a coin into a small cup. Imtiaz flicked with a steady hand and good aim. He got the most coins in and won.
payload.title: Imtiaz wins the coin flicking game
decoys: A steady hand wins the game

payload.passage: Sara went to the market to buy a gift for her friend. She looked at hair clips, books, and small puzzles. After a long look around, she picked a story book with pictures. Sara hoped her friend would love the surprise.
payload.title: Buying a Gift for a Friend
decoys: She picked a picture story book.

payload.passage: Ishaan enjoys building bird nests out of twigs and grass. He weaves them into a small round cup. He places the nest gently in the garden bush. Ishaan hopes a little bird will come to live in it.
payload.title: Ishaan Builds a Twig Nest
decoys: He places it in a bush.

payload.passage: Aditya found a room about flying machines at the museum. Old planes hung from the high ceiling. A board told how the first plane flew long ago. Aditya dreamed of flying high above the clouds one day.
payload.title: Old Planes at the Museum
decoys: Old planes hung from the ceiling.

payload.passage: Aditya found a room full of old maps at the museum. The maps showed cities and seas drawn long ago. Some places had different names than they do now. Aditya traced the old roads with his finger on the glass.
payload.title: Old Maps at the Museum

payload.passage: Anaya loves to make her own picture books. She draws a story on folded sheets of paper. She staples the pages to keep them together. Anaya reads her little books to her younger cousins.
payload.title: Anaya Makes Picture Books

payload.passage: Ravi enjoys making little kites from leaves and sticks. He finds a big strong leaf in the garden. He ties it to a thin stick with a long thread. Ravi loves running with his leaf kite in the breeze.
payload.title: Ravi Makes Kites from Leaves
decoys: He uses a big strong leaf.

payload.passage: Karan enjoys baking small breads with his grandmother. They knead the dough and let it rise. They shape little rolls and bake them golden. Karan loves the smell of fresh bread filling the kitchen.
payload.title: Karan Bakes Bread with Grandmother

payload.passage: Aarav found a room about the human body at the museum. There was a big model showing bones and the heart. A screen let him press buttons to learn more. Aarav was amazed at how cleverly the body is made.
payload.title: Learning About the Body
decoys: He pressed buttons on a screen.

payload.passage: Every morning before school, Dinesh runs around the park. He started with just one round and felt very tired. After many weeks of practice, he could run five rounds easily. Now he is the fastest runner in his class.
payload.title: Dinesh trains to become a fast runner
decoys: He runs in the park every morning

payload.passage: Divya saw the maid struggling with a tall stack of plates. She quickly took half the plates in her own hands. Then she walked carefully to the kitchen with them. The maid smiled and said thank you for the help.
payload.title: Divya helps carry the heavy plates
decoys: The maid had a tall stack of plates
The maid said thank you for help
We should be kind to everyone

payload.passage: Kabir collects pretty stones from his walks. He keeps them in a glass jar on his desk. Some stones are smooth, some shiny, and some have spots. Kabir likes to show his stone jar to anyone who visits.
payload.title: Kabir's Collection of Stones
decoys: He keeps them in a glass jar.

payload.passage: The school garden had become dry and full of weeds. The children decided to make it green again. Some pulled the weeds while others watered the plants. By the weekend the garden was full of colourful flowers.
payload.title: Children bring the school garden back to life
decoys: The garden was full of weeds

payload.passage: A girls' basketball team was new and lost their first match. They felt low but did not stop trying. They practised passing and shooting after school. In the next match they finally won.
payload.title: The basketball team practises and wins
decoys: Practice turns a loss into a win

payload.passage: Sara loves to make her own little flip books. She draws a tiny picture on each page. The pictures change slightly from one to the next. When Sara flips them fast, the drawings seem to move.
payload.title: Sara Makes Moving Flip Books

payload.passage: Sneha buried her brother's feet in the warm sand. She piled the sand high until only his toes showed. He wiggled free with a laugh, sending sand flying. They both rolled in the sand and giggled for a long time.
payload.title: Burying Feet in the Sand

payload.passage: At the night zoo, the children visited after dark. They saw owls, bats, and a sleepy slow loris with big round eyes. A guide used a soft red light so the animals were not bothered. Arjun learned that some animals are awake only at night.
payload.title: A Visit to the Night Zoo
decoys: The guide used a red light.

payload.passage: When Imran broke his arm, he could not write for many days. His friends took turns to write his notes for him. They also carried his bag and opened his tiffin box. Imran said he was lucky to have such friends.
payload.title: Friends help Imran with his broken arm
decoys: Imran could not write for days
They carried his bag for him
Good friends are a great blessing

payload.passage: Ananya loves to bake with her mother on Sundays. They mix flour, sugar, and butter in a big bowl. Last week they baked soft cookies shaped like stars. The whole house smelled sweet while the cookies baked.
payload.title: Baking Cookies with Mother

payload.passage: Aarav learned to fly kites from his grandfather. They run the strong thread between their fingers just right. On windy days they fly bright kites from the terrace. Aarav loves the long evenings of flying kites together.
payload.title: Aarav Learns to Fly Kites

payload.passage: An old man could not read the bus number from far. He stood worried that he might miss his bus. A girl beside him read out each bus number aloud. She helped him board the right bus on time.
payload.title: A girl helps an old man board
decoys: He could not read from far

payload.passage: It started to rain during the football match, and the field grew slippery. Many players slipped and fell in the mud. But the children laughed and kept playing happily. They said the muddy match was the most fun ever.
payload.title: Children enjoy the muddy football match
decoys: Many players fell in the mud
Rain can make games more fun

payload.passage: Sneha visited the camel at the zoo on a hot day. The big camel had a tall hump on its back. A board said camels can go many days without water. Sneha learned that camels are made for living in the dry desert.
payload.title: The Camel at the Zoo
decoys: The camel had a tall hump.
Sneha visited on a hot day.

payload.passage: Meera loves to make sun catchers for the window. She glues bits of coloured paper onto clear sheets. She hangs them where the sunlight pours in. Meera loves how the colours glow when the sun shines through.
payload.title: Meera Makes Window Sun Catchers
decoys: She hangs them in the sun.

payload.passage: Priya watched the tide slowly come in at the beach. Bit by bit, the water crept up the sand. Soon her sandcastle was close to the edge of the waves. Priya moved her things higher to keep them dry.
payload.title: Watching the Tide Come In
decoys: Her castle was near the waves.

payload.passage: Geeta had saved her pocket money for many weeks. She wanted to buy a pretty doll she had seen. Then she heard that a flood had hurt many families. So Geeta gave all her savings to help them instead.
payload.title: Geeta donates her savings to flood victims
decoys: Geeta wanted to buy a doll
She had saved for many weeks

payload.passage: The park bench near the temple was broken and dusty. Children had nowhere clean to sit and rest. Kabir told his father, and they fixed the bench together. Now everyone in the colony enjoys a clean place to sit.
payload.title: Kabir helps fix the broken park bench
decoys: The bench was broken and dusty
He told his father about it
Public things should be looked after

payload.passage: Diya enjoys keeping a scrapbook of her trips. She sticks in tickets, leaves, and small photos. She writes a few lines about each place she visits. Diya loves looking back through all her happy memories.
payload.title: Diya Keeps a Trip Scrapbook
decoys: She sticks in tickets and leaves.

payload.passage: Vikram enjoys drawing comic strips in his notebook. He draws little boxes with funny pictures inside. He writes the words his characters say in bubbles. Vikram's comics make his classmates laugh out loud.
payload.title: Vikram Draws Comic Strips

payload.passage: Ishaan loves to make shadow puppets from card. He cuts out shapes of animals and people. He holds them up to a lamp behind a white sheet. Ishaan puts on shadow plays for his family at night.
payload.title: Ishaan Makes Shadow Puppets
decoys: He uses a lamp and sheet.

payload.passage: Meera loves to make her own paper crowns. She cuts zigzag points along a strip of card. She sticks on shiny paper gems and glitter. Meera wears her sparkling crown when she plays the queen.
payload.title: Meera Makes Paper Crowns

payload.passage: The little boy could not reach the tap to wash his hands. It was placed too high for him. Preeti lifted him gently so he could reach the water. He washed his hands and said thank you to her.
payload.title: Preeti helps a small boy reach the tap
decoys: The tap was placed too high
Helping little ones is very kind

payload.passage: A new bat and ball were given to the class for games. Some children wanted to keep them for themselves. But the captain said everyone must get a chance. They made a fair turn list and all played happily.
payload.title: The class shares new sports gear fairly

payload.passage: The market had a corner with many kinds of nuts. There were almonds, cashews, and small brown walnuts. Sara watched the seller weigh them on a small scale. Her mother bought a mix to add to the evening sweets.
payload.title: The Nut Stall at the Market

payload.passage: Two friends had a balloon keepy-uppy game indoors. They had to keep the balloon from touching the floor. Esha tapped it up gently again and again. Her balloon stayed up the longest and she won.
payload.title: Esha keeps the balloon up the longest
decoys: They kept it off the floor

payload.passage: Mira loved to play badminton with her father each evening. She could not reach the high shots at first. Her father showed her how to jump and swing. Now she returns even the highest shuttle.
payload.title: Mira learns to reach high shuttles
decoys: She could not reach high shots
A parent makes a good coach

payload.passage: The beach had little pools of water left among the rocks. Ishaan looked into them and found tiny fish and crabs. The pools were like small windows into the sea. Ishaan spent a long time peering into each one.
payload.title: Exploring Rock Pools at the Beach
decoys: He found tiny fish and crabs.
The beach is by the sea.

payload.passage: Aarav saw a crab on the wet sand near the water. It had a hard shell and ran sideways very fast. When Aarav came close, the crab hid inside a small hole. He waited quietly, hoping it would come out again.
payload.title: A Crab on the Beach Sand
decoys: It hid in a small hole.

payload.passage: Sneha enjoys learning to draw birds step by step. She starts with a circle and adds a beak. Slowly the bird takes shape on her paper. Sneha is proud that her birds look better every week.
payload.title: Sneha Learns to Draw Birds

payload.passage: Karan enjoys learning to skip with a long rope. He turns the rope and jumps over it each time. At first he tripped after only a few jumps. Now Karan can skip many times without stopping.
payload.title: Karan Learns to Skip Rope
decoys: He turns the rope and jumps.

payload.passage: Kabir enjoys building bridges out of ice-cream sticks. He glues the sticks into strong shapes. He tests each bridge by placing small toys on top. Kabir is happy when his bridge holds without falling down.
payload.title: Kabir Builds Stick Bridges

payload.passage: Two friends played a game of carrom in the evening. The board was dusty, so they wiped it clean first. Nikhil pocketed the red queen with a tricky shot. He covered it and won the carrom game.
payload.title: Nikhil pockets the queen and wins carrom

payload.passage: A small girl was crying because her balloon flew away. It got stuck high up in a tree branch. Kunal climbed up carefully and brought the balloon down. The little girl laughed and thanked him.
payload.title: Kunal rescues the girl's stuck balloon
decoys: The balloon got stuck in a tree
A small help can bring big smiles

payload.passage: Vikram loves to build dams in the garden after rain. He piles up mud and stones to hold the water. He makes little channels for the water to flow. Vikram watches the water rush along the paths he made.
payload.title: Vikram Builds Mud Dams
decoys: He piles up mud and stones.

payload.passage: After the heavy rain, a stray puppy was shivering near the gate. It was wet, cold, and very hungry. Shreya wrapped it in an old towel and gave it warm milk. She kept it safe until its owner came looking for it.
payload.title: Shreya rescues a shivering stray puppy
decoys: The puppy was wet and cold

payload.passage: Two boys raced their cycles around the colony park. They pedalled hard along the curving path. Naresh took the turns smoothly without slowing. He crossed the line first and won.
payload.title: Naresh wins the cycle park race

payload.passage: Shalu loved gymnastics and practised her cartwheels daily. At first she wobbled and fell on the soft mat. She kept trying until her cartwheels were smooth. At the show, everyone clapped for her perfect turns.
payload.title: Shalu masters her cartwheels
decoys: She wobbled and fell at first

payload.passage: The children played a game of statue in the park. When the leader shouted, everyone had to freeze still. Toya stood like a stone without even blinking. She held it the longest and won the game.
payload.title: Toya wins the statue game

payload.passage: Aarav enjoys learning magic tricks with coins. He practises making a coin vanish in his hand. He shows the trick to anyone who will watch. Aarav loves the look of wonder on their faces.
payload.title: Aarav Learns Coin Magic

payload.passage: At the market, the fish seller called out his prices loudly. Fresh fish lay on a bed of ice to keep cool. People crowded around to pick the best ones. Anjali held her nose because of the strong fishy smell.
payload.title: The Busy Fish Seller's Stall

payload.passage: The girls played a long game of hopscotch on the road. They drew the squares with white chalk. Nina hopped through all the squares without a mistake. She won the game and drew a new round.
payload.title: Nina wins the hopscotch game

payload.passage: A baby goat got its leg stuck in a wire fence. It bleated loudly in pain and fear. Joy carefully bent the wire and freed its leg. The little goat hopped away to its mother.
payload.title: Joy frees the trapped baby goat
decoys: It hopped away to its mother
Saving animals is a kind deed

payload.passage: A girl's hair ribbon flew off into a muddy ditch. She felt sad as it was her favourite one. Her friend found a stick and lifted it out gently. They washed it clean at the tap together.
payload.title: A friend rescues the lost ribbon
decoys: The ribbon flew into a ditch
They washed it at the tap

payload.passage: Veer found a room about the sea at the museum. Glass cases held shells, coral, and a model whale. A screen showed fish swimming deep in the dark water. Veer learned how many strange creatures live in the sea.
payload.title: The Sea Room at the Museum

payload.passage: Ananya loves to learn folk songs from her grandmother. They sing together every evening on the terrace. Ananya remembers the words after singing many times. Now she can sing three whole songs all by herself.
payload.title: Ananya Learns Folk Songs

payload.passage: Ishaan found a small theatre inside the museum. A short film told the story of an old city. He sat in the dark and watched the screen come alive. Ishaan learned how that city grew over hundreds of years.
payload.title: Watching a Film at the Museum
decoys: The film was about an old city.

payload.passage: Pooja noticed that a girl in class had forgotten her lunch. The girl sat sadly with an empty box. Pooja opened her own tiffin and shared her sandwiches. The two girls ate happily and became good friends.
payload.title: Pooja shares her lunch with a friend
decoys: The girl had an empty lunch box
Pooja had sandwiches in her tiffin
Sharing food is a kind act

payload.passage: Aditya has a hobby of building paper houses. He draws windows and doors before he folds. He even adds tiny paper furniture inside. Aditya is slowly making a whole paper village on his desk.
payload.title: Aditya Builds a Paper Village

payload.passage: Two cricket teams played in the bright afternoon sun. The match was close and every run mattered. Manav ran quickly between the wickets without tiring. His fast running helped his team win by two runs.
payload.title: Manav's quick running wins the match

payload.passage: Diya went to the stationery stall to buy school things. She picked out pencils, erasers, and a bright new notebook. The seller put everything into a small paper bag. Diya could not wait to use her new things at school.
payload.title: Buying School Things at the Market
decoys: The seller used a paper bag.

payload.passage: On a rainy day, the children could not go out to play. So they took out the carrom board instead. Vinod aimed carefully and pocketed all his coins first. He won the game and everyone wanted to play again.
payload.title: Vinod wins the carrom game indoors

payload.passage: Tarun could not skip the rope even once at first. The rope kept hitting his feet and he tripped. He practised every day in his backyard. After two weeks, he could skip a hundred times without stopping.
payload.title: Tarun learns to skip the rope
decoys: The rope kept hitting his feet

payload.passage: A small boy was scared to walk past a barking dog. He stood frozen on the footpath and would not move. A kind girl held his hand and walked beside him. They passed the dog safely and the boy smiled.
payload.title: A girl helps past the barking dog

payload.passage: At the zoo, the elephant was the biggest animal of all. It splashed water with its long trunk and flapped its wide ears. A baby elephant stayed close to its mother the whole time. Everyone clapped when the big elephant gave a loud trumpet.
payload.title: The Big Elephant at the Zoo
decoys: The elephant splashed water with its trunk.
A baby elephant stayed near its mother.

payload.passage: Rohan and his friends went on the bumper cars. They drove little cars and bumped gently into each other. Everyone laughed each time the cars knocked together. The bumper cars were the best fun of the whole fair.
payload.title: Bumper Cars at the Fair

payload.passage: Meera visited the plant nursery at the edge of the market. Rows of green plants sat in little pots and bags. A man helped her pick a plant with bright red flowers. Meera carried it home to brighten up her balcony.
payload.title: Buying a Plant at the Nursery
decoys: She picked one with red flowers.

payload.passage: The book stall in the market was Ravi's favourite spot. Old and new books were piled high on the table. He looked for a comic about a brave hero. Ravi found one for a good price and read it on the way home.
payload.title: The Book Stall at the Market

payload.passage: Aarav builds small boats that really float. He uses bits of wood, glue, and a paper sail. He tests each boat in a tub full of water. Aarav loves watching his little boats sail across the tub.
payload.title: Aarav Builds Floating Boats
decoys: He tests them in a tub.

payload.passage: Meera visited the sweet shop at the market with her uncle. Trays of sweets sat behind the clean glass case. She could not decide which one looked the nicest. In the end, her uncle bought a box of mixed sweets to share.
payload.title: Choosing Sweets at the Market Shop
decoys: Her uncle bought a mixed box.

payload.passage: The zoo had a long row of cages full of bright birds. There were tiny finches, talking mynas, and golden canaries. One myna copied the words a visitor said. Diya laughed when the clever bird called out hello to her.
payload.title: The Talking Myna at the Zoo

payload.passage: During the heat, the milkman's cycle chain came off the wheel. He could not fix it with his oily hands. A helpful man stopped and put the chain back on. The milkman thanked him and rode away.
payload.title: A man helps fix the milkman's cycle
decoys: The chain came off the wheel

payload.passage: Sneha flew a kite on the windy beach. The strong wind lifted the kite high into the blue sky. She let out the string until the kite was tiny and far. Sneha held on tight so the wind would not take it away.
payload.title: Flying a Kite at the Beach

payload.passage: When the old temple wall needed a fresh coat of paint, the colony joined in. Fathers held the ladders steady and mothers mixed the paint. The children passed the brushes and cleaned the spills. By Sunday the wall looked bright and new.
payload.title: The colony paints the temple wall together
decoys: People can do great things together

payload.passage: Asma saw an ant struggling in a small puddle of water. The tiny ant could not climb out alone. She gently placed a dry leaf near it. The ant crawled onto the leaf and reached dry ground safely.
payload.title: Asma saves a tiny ant from water
decoys: The ant struggled in a puddle
She placed a dry leaf near it
Even tiny lives are worth saving

payload.passage: An old fruit seller could not push his heavy cart up the slope. The wheels kept slipping on the road. Three boys from the colony came and pushed from behind. Together they got the cart safely to the top.
payload.title: Boys help push the fruit seller's cart

payload.passage: The class played a memory chain game in a circle. Each child added a word and repeated the list. Ria remembered the whole long chain of words. She was the last one left and won the game.
payload.title: Ria wins the memory chain game
decoys: She was the last one left
A sharp memory wins this game

payload.passage: Aditya watched a boat sail far out on the sea. Its white sail puffed full with the wind. It grew smaller and smaller as it moved away. Aditya waved until the little boat was just a dot.
payload.title: Watching a Boat Sail Away

payload.passage: The children played a fun ball balancing game in the hall. They had to balance a ball on a bat while walking. Harini walked steadily without dropping the ball. She reached the line first and won.
payload.title: Harini wins the ball balancing game
decoys: They balanced a ball on a bat

payload.passage: The children played blind man's buff in the garden. One child was blindfolded and had to catch the others. Sohan listened to every soft footstep around him. He caught a friend and won his turn.
payload.title: Sohan wins at blind man's buff
decoys: Sharp ears help in this game

payload.passage: During the festival, the watchman of the building had to work all night. He looked tired and had not eaten. Neha's family packed him a warm dinner and a sweet. The watchman was touched by their kind thought.
payload.title: Neha's family feeds the tired watchman

payload.passage: The children played a balloon stamping game in the hall. Each child had a balloon tied to one ankle. They tried to stamp others' balloons while saving their own. Karan kept his balloon safe and won the game.
payload.title: Karan saves his balloon and wins

payload.passage: On market day, the lanes were packed with people. Sellers shouted, carts rolled, and bells rang from the cycle riders. Aditya held tight to his mother's hand so he would not get lost. The busy market was loud but full of life.
payload.title: A Busy Day at the Market

payload.passage: Anaya enjoys making puppets from paper bags. She glues on paper ears, eyes, and a nose. She slips her hand inside to make them talk. Anaya's paper bag puppets put on funny little shows.
payload.title: Anaya Makes Paper Bag Puppets

payload.passage: The reptile keeper held a baby crocodile for the children to see. He showed its sharp little teeth and rough skin. He told them crocodiles can stay still for hours waiting for food. The children listened with wide eyes and many questions.
payload.title: Learning About Baby Crocodiles

payload.passage: Deepak was a fast bowler in his school team. He ran in quickly and bowled with great speed. The batsman could not see the ball in time. Deepak took three wickets and helped his team win.
payload.title: Deepak's fast bowling wins the game

payload.passage: Anil and Sunil had a friendly arm wrestling match. Anil was stronger but Sunil was very clever. Sunil used a quick trick to push Anil's arm down. They both laughed and shook hands after the game.
payload.title: Sunil wins arm wrestling with a clever trick

payload.passage: Anjali enjoys pressing flowers in heavy books. She picks small flowers and lays them flat between the pages. After many days, the flowers turn dry and thin. Anjali sticks the pressed flowers into a pretty scrapbook.
payload.title: Anjali Presses Flowers in Books

payload.passage: The children built a sandcastle game on the school beach trip. They split into groups to make the tallest tower. Roshni's group worked together and packed the sand tight. Their castle stood the tallest of all.
payload.title: Roshni's group builds the tallest castle

payload.passage: A girls' football team trained hard for the big final. They passed and ran together every day. On the final day they played as one strong team. They scored two goals and lifted the cup.
payload.title: Teamwork helps the girls win the final
decoys: A team wins by playing together

payload.passage: Ravi enjoys making a model rocket from a bottle. He tapes paper fins around the bottom. He draws a sharp paper cone for the top. Ravi pretends his bottle rocket blasts off into space.
payload.title: Ravi Builds a Model Rocket

payload.passage: A small puppy followed the school children every day. One day it looked thin and very hungry. The children saved a little food from their tiffins. They fed the puppy together and it grew strong.
payload.title: Children feed a hungry school puppy
decoys: Caring for strays is a good habit

payload.passage: Priya loves to make her own wrapping paper. She stamps shapes onto plain sheets with cut sponges. She uses bright paint in red, blue, and green. Priya wraps her gifts in the cheerful paper she made.
payload.title: Priya Makes Her Own Wrapping Paper

payload.passage: The school had a fancy obstacle race on sports day. The children had to crawl, jump, and run through it. Sanjay was quick at every part of the course. He finished first and won a bright ribbon.
payload.title: Sanjay wins the obstacle race
decoys: They had to crawl and jump

payload.passage: The class fan stopped working on a very hot day. The children sat sweating and could not focus. A boy fanned the youngest child with a notebook. Soon a worker came and repaired the fan.
payload.title: A boy fans a younger child
decoys: Caring for others in heat is kind

payload.passage: An old couple struggled to carry their bags up the railway bridge. The steps were many and steep. Two young boys took the bags and climbed up for them. The couple blessed the boys for their help.
payload.title: Boys help an old couple cross the bridge
decoys: Helping elders is a fine deed

payload.passage: Aditya likes to take photos with his father's old camera. He looks for birds, flowers, and funny clouds. He clicks a picture whenever something catches his eye. Aditya hopes to fill a whole album with his best photos.
payload.title: Aditya's Hobby of Taking Photos
decoys: He looks for birds and flowers.

payload.passage: Ishaan visited the deer park inside the zoo. Soft brown deer with spotted backs walked freely among the trees. Some deer came close to nibble grass from his open hand. Ishaan felt very happy to be so near the gentle animals.
payload.title: Feeding Deer at the Zoo

payload.passage: Karan likes to build models from old cardboard boxes. He cut, folded, and glued the pieces with great care. This time he made a tall tower with little windows. Karan felt proud of the strong tower he had built.
payload.title: Karan Builds a Cardboard Tower

payload.passage: Rohan enjoys building a tall tower of wooden blocks. He pulls out one block at a time without it falling. The tower wobbles more with every move. Rohan holds his breath until his block is safely out.
payload.title: Rohan Plays the Block Tower Game
decoys: He pulls out one block at a time.

payload.passage: Veer built a long sand wall to keep the waves out. He patted the sand down hard with both hands. The wall held back the small waves for a while. But a big wave finally broke right through it.
payload.title: Veer's Wall Against the Waves

payload.passage: It started to rain heavily as the children walked home. Only Simran had remembered to bring an umbrella. She called her classmate Rekha to walk under it with her. They reached home dry and giggling all the way.
payload.title: Simran shares her umbrella in the rain

payload.passage: Gaurav saw a younger student crying near the gate after school. The little boy could not find his school bus. Gaurav held his hand and took him to the teacher on duty. The teacher found the right bus very quickly.
payload.title: Gaurav helps a lost little boy
decoys: The little boy could not find his bus
The teacher found the bus quickly
Older children should guide the younger

payload.passage: The bear at the zoo was busy looking for honey. It used its strong paws to dig and turn over logs. A keeper had hidden treats inside a hollow tree. Sara loved watching the clever bear search for its tasty snack.
payload.title: The Bear Hunts for Honey
decoys: Treats were hidden in a tree.

payload.passage: The zoo had a special place just for baby animals. There was a tiny deer, a small bear cub, and a fluffy duckling. A helper fed them milk from a bottle. Everyone said the baby animals were the cutest part of the whole zoo.
payload.title: The Baby Animal Corner
decoys: There was a small bear cub.

payload.passage: A blind beggar dropped his coins on the busy footpath. He tapped around but could not find them. Ajay knelt down and gathered every coin for him. He placed the coins gently back in the man's bowl.
payload.title: Ajay returns the blind man's coins
decoys: He placed coins in the bowl
Helping the blind is very kind

payload.passage: Two friends raced their paper boats in the rainwater. The water flowed fast along the gutter. Kabir's boat was light and moved the quickest. His boat reached the drain first and won the race.
payload.title: Kabir's paper boat wins the race

payload.passage: Riya enjoys making colourful floor patterns at her doorstep. She draws curves and dots first, using a little chalk. Then she fills in each shape with bright coloured powder. Riya loves how the floor pattern brightens up the whole house.
payload.title: Riya Makes Doorstep Floor Patterns

payload.passage: On sports day, Vinay was the slowest in the running race. But he never missed his morning practice runs. Week after week he grew faster and stronger. This year, he came second in the same race.
payload.title: Vinay improves his race timing

payload.passage: The owl at the zoo sat very still on a high branch. Its big round eyes seemed to watch everyone below. A keeper said owls hunt at night and sleep in the day. Aarav waited a long time to see the quiet owl blink.
payload.title: The Quiet Owl at the Zoo
decoys: The owl had big round eyes.

payload.passage: The classroom window would not shut, and rain came in. The desks near it were getting wet. Two boys pushed the stuck window closed together. They wiped the wet desks with a cloth.
payload.title: Boys shut the stuck window in the rain
decoys: Quick action keeps the class dry

payload.passage: Two cricket teams played a hard and close match. At the end, one team won and the other lost. Both teams shook hands and said well played. They learned that playing fair is more important than winning.
payload.title: Both teams show good sportsmanship
decoys: Fair play is better than winning

payload.passage: A skipping competition was held during the school break. Children skipped fast to see who could last longest. Bina skipped without missing for two whole minutes. She won the prize for the most skips.

decoys: The meadow grass turns golden in autumn
Nature looks different in each season
Butterflies love a flowery summer meadow

decoys: The big words slowed Reema down at first
Books open the door to every kind of knowledge
Reema read two pages each night before sleep

decoys: The curled corner caught their feet
A small fix can prevent a nasty fall
Mother taped the corners down flat

Plants do many clever things to live
Green leaves use sunlight to make food

decoys: He clears the rubbish from the drain

payload.title: How a signal operator guides the trains
decoys: He sets the signals to green or red
Many helpers keep us moving safely

payload.passage: The school's gate often stayed locked because the watchman lost the key. Children waited outside until a spare was hunted down. A watchman keeps every school safe and secure
A duplicate key was kept in the office

payload.title: How a neighbourhood doctor brings care close
decoys: He examines each patient who comes
Many helpers look after our health
A fever often means rest is needed

payload.passage: A pumpkin starts its life as a bright yellow flower on a creeping vine. After a bee visits the flower, a tiny green fruit forms at its base. payload.title: How a pumpkin grows from a flower
decoys: A ripe pumpkin turns a deep orange colour
Vines grow many kinds of fruit
Pumpkins are cooked into many dishes

A small change can fix a big daily trouble

payload.title: A water filter solved the bad-tasting water
decoys: Children came to class thirsty and tired
Clean water is the right of every person
The principal fitted a filter on the tank

payload.passage: Lightning and thunder always happen during the same storm. Lightning is a sudden flash of electricity that jumps through the sky. decoys: Lightning heats the air very quickly
Storms can be loud and exciting
Heavy rain often falls during a storm

payload.title: How bees dance to share food news
decoys: A worker bee dances on the honeycomb
Insects talk to each other in many ways
Bees gather sweet nectar from flowers

payload.passage: A cloud may look soft and solid, but it is really tiny drops of water. The sun warms water on Earth until it rises as invisible vapour. High up where the air is cool, the vapour turns back into tiny droplets. Millions of these droplets float together and we see them as a cloud. So every fluffy cloud is made of countless tiny water drops.
payload.title: A cloud is made of tiny water drops
decoys: Water vapour rises until the air cools it
The sky changes its look every day
Rain falls down to fill our lakes

payload.passage: Vikram wanted to balance on his cricket bat handle as a fun trick. He tried for days and the bat toppled over again and again. payload.title: Steady focus helped Vikram balance the bat

Cricket teaches children patience and teamwork
Vikram balanced the bat on its handle

decoys: Meera's neat pages were ruined by scribbles

Meera had to copy her notes again

Vegetables are cheaper after a good harvest

Aryan performed at a family get-together

payload.passage: Summer in many Indian cities can be very hot and dry. The sun beats down from a clear sky and the ground feels burning to touch. decoys: People drink cool water and juice in summer
The weather is different in every season
Mangoes ripen and taste sweet in summer

Aniket used a ruler to underline steps

Clean clothes help keep us healthy

Old trees give shade to many travellers

payload.passage: A bookseller runs a shop full of books for the whole neighbourhood. He arranges the books neatly by subject on his shelves. When a customer asks for a story or a textbook, he helps them find it. He keeps new books coming in so there is always something to read. So a bookseller's work is to bring good books to readers.
payload.title: How a bookseller brings books to readers
decoys: He arranges books neatly by subject

payload.passage: Kavya struggled to learn the names of all the planets in order. They kept slipping out of her head right before the science quiz. She made up a funny sentence using the first letter of each planet. The silly sentence stuck in her mind and the order came easily. Kavya answered every planet question in the quiz without any trouble.
payload.title: A memory sentence helped Kavya learn the planets
decoys: The planet names slipped out of Kavya's head
Space is the most exciting subject to study
Kavya had a science quiz coming up soon

payload.passage: The roots of a plant do quiet but vital work underground. They grip the soil so the plant does not fall over in the wind. They also drink up water and food from the earth around them. This water travels up the stem to feed the leaves and flowers. So a plant depends on its hidden roots to live and grow.
payload.title: Hidden roots keep a plant alive
decoys: Roots grip the soil against the wind
Green leaves make food using sunlight

payload.passage: Diya often missed the school van because she could not find her socks. Searching for them every morning made her late and flustered. She started keeping a pair of clean socks ready by her shoes at night. Each morning she slipped them on without any hunting. Diya caught the van on time every single day after that.
payload.title: Keeping socks ready solved Diya's missed van
decoys: Searching for socks made Diya late
Planning ahead solves all morning problems
Diya kept socks ready by her shoes

payload.passage: Autumn is a season of slow change and rich colours. The hot summer fades and the air turns cool and crisp. Leaves on many trees turn yellow, orange, and red before they fall. Farmers gather the crops they planted earlier in the year. So autumn is a time of harvest and falling leaves.
payload.title: Autumn brings harvest and falling leaves
decoys: Leaves turn yellow, orange, and red in autumn
Every season looks different from the last
Cool air feels nice after a hot summer

payload.passage: A sand dune is a hill of sand that slowly moves across a desert. The wind picks up loose grains and carries them up one side. The grains tumble down the far side and pile up there. Bit by bit, the whole dune creeps along in the direction of the wind. So a sand dune is a hill that the wind slowly walks across the land.
payload.title: How the wind moves a sand dune
decoys: Grains tumble down the far side of the dune
Camels can walk easily over soft sand

payload.passage: Pooja tried to learn a few card tricks to amaze her cousins. The cards kept slipping and her tricks were easy to spot at first. She practised in front of the mirror until her hands moved smoothly. Each failed trick taught her exactly which move to hide better. At the family dinner her cousins gasped, sure that real magic had happened.
payload.title: Mirror practice made Pooja's card tricks smooth
decoys: Pooja's cards kept slipping at first
Magic tricks can fool absolutely everyone around
Pooja wanted to amaze her many cousins

payload.passage: Laksh wanted to learn how to play a tune on water-filled glasses. His first notes were all the same, dull, and tuneless. He poured different amounts of water until each glass sang a new note. Tapping them in order, he found the notes of a real song. Laksh played a little melody on his glasses for the science fair.
payload.title: Adjusting the water taught Laksh the glass melody
decoys: Laksh's first notes were dull and the same
Science fairs are exciting for every student
Laksh played his melody at the science fair

payload.passage: A school watchman keeps the children safe inside the school gate. He opens the gate in the morning and shuts it once classes begin. He checks anyone who comes during school hours. He makes sure no child wanders out onto the busy road. So a watchman's work is to guard the school and its children.
payload.title: How a watchman guards the school gate
decoys: He shuts the gate once classes begin
The road outside school is busy

payload.passage: The phases of the moon change night by night across a month. Sometimes the moon is a thin curved sliver in the sky. A few nights later more of it shows, until it becomes a full round circle. Then it shrinks again, getting thinner each night, until it nearly vanishes. So the moon seems to change its shape all month long.
payload.title: How the moon changes shape each month
decoys: A full moon looks like a round circle
The night sky is full of wonders
The moon gives soft light at night

payload.passage: A baby elephant relies on its herd from the moment it is born. It can stand within an hour but still needs much help and care. The mother and other elephants guard it and guide it as it walks. It drinks its mother's milk and slowly learns to find its own food. So a young elephant grows up safely inside a caring herd.
payload.title: A baby elephant grows up in a herd
decoys: A baby elephant can stand within an hour
Animals look after their young in many ways
Elephants use their trunks to pick up food

payload.passage: A pond can freeze on top yet stay alive underneath in winter. When the cold deepens, a layer of ice forms across the surface. This ice acts like a lid that keeps the cold out of the water below. Fish and frogs stay in the slightly warmer water under the ice. So a frozen lid keeps a pond's life safe through winter.
payload.title: How ice keeps a pond alive in winter
decoys: Fish stay in the water under the ice
Children sometimes slide on frozen ponds

payload.passage: The classroom's window curtain kept falling down on the children's heads. The loose rod slipped from its bracket whenever the wind blew. A worker screwed the bracket back tightly into the wall. The curtain rod held firm and stopped falling after that. The children sat safely without curtains dropping on them.
payload.title: Fixing the bracket solved the falling curtain
decoys: The rod slipped whenever the wind blew
A safe classroom is the right of every child
A worker screwed the bracket tightly

payload.passage: A traffic police officer keeps the busy roads in order. He stands at the crossing where many cars and bikes meet. With clear hand signals he tells some to stop and others to go. He also helps children and old people cross the road safely. So a traffic officer keeps the roads safe and moving smoothly.
payload.title: How a traffic officer keeps roads safe
decoys: The officer uses clear hand signals
Many helpers serve the busy city
Cars must stop when the light turns red

payload.passage: A sunflower seems to follow the sun across the sky each day. In the morning the young flower faces east where the sun comes up. As the sun moves across the sky, the flower slowly turns to keep facing it. By evening the flower is pointing west towards the setting sun. This slow turning helps the sunflower soak up as much sunlight as it can.
payload.title: A sunflower turns to follow the sun
decoys: In the morning the flower faces east
Plants do many clever things to live
Sunflower seeds are tasty and good to eat

payload.passage: A bank clerk helps people keep their money safe and in order. When you bring money to save, he counts it and writes it in your book. He hands out money when you need to take some out. He answers questions and helps fill in the right forms. So a bank clerk's work is to look after people's money carefully.
payload.title: How a bank clerk handles our money
decoys: He counts the money and writes it down
Many helpers serve people every day
Banks stay closed on most holidays

payload.passage: The school staircase grew dangerously crowded when the bell rang. Children pushed and a few small ones nearly tumbled down. The teachers made one staircase only for going up and one for coming down. The crowding eased as the children moved in one smooth direction. Now everyone walks the stairs safely without any pushing.
payload.title: Separate stairs solved the crowding danger
decoys: A few small children nearly tumbled down
Crowds are always dangerous in any building
The teachers split the staircase usage

payload.passage: Sparrows once hopped about every Indian street, but now they are harder to find. Tall glass buildings have replaced the old houses where they nested. The hedges and small fields where they found insects have shrunk away. With fewer homes and less food, their numbers have quietly dropped. Putting up nest boxes and growing native plants can welcome the sparrows back.
payload.title: Why sparrows are disappearing from our streets
decoys: Nest boxes can welcome sparrows back

payload.passage: A simple shift to a cloth handkerchief saves more than it seems. Paper tissues are used once and tossed, and making them takes trees, water and energy. A cloth handkerchief tucked in a pocket can be washed and used for years. Over a lifetime, this swap spares many trees and bins of waste. Choosing cloth over paper is an easy, daily way to tread lightly on the earth.
payload.title: Why a cloth handkerchief is kinder to nature
decoys: A cloth handkerchief can be used for years

payload.passage: Wave goodbye in front of a still pond and the water shows your moving hand. A calm pond acts almost like a mirror. Light from your hand strikes the smooth water and bounces straight back up into your eyes. This bounced light forms a picture, which is the reflection you see. The moment the wind ripples the surface, the smooth picture breaks into shimmering pieces.
payload.title: Why a still pond reflects like a mirror
decoys: Light bounces off the smooth water
Ponds are home to many creatures
Wind ripples break up the reflection

payload.passage: Why does a bridge have small gaps between its sections of road? On a hot day the metal and concrete of a bridge spread out and grow longer. On a cold day they shrink back and grow shorter. If there were no gaps, the spreading parts would push hard against each other and crack. The gaps give the bridge room to grow and shrink without breaking.
payload.title: Why bridges are built with small gaps
decoys: Metal spreads out on a hot day
Bridges are amazing feats of building
Gaps give the bridge room to grow

payload.passage: A cat's eyes seem to glow when light falls on them at night. Behind the cat's eye lies a shiny layer, almost like a tiny mirror. Light enters the eye and, if it is not caught the first time, the mirror bounces it back through. This gives the cat a second chance to use that light and see in near darkness. The leftover light that escapes back out is what makes the eyes appear to glow.
payload.title: Why a cat's eyes glow in the dark
decoys: A shiny layer sits behind the cat's eye
A cat can see well in near darkness

payload.passage: A heap of vegetable peels and dry leaves can become black gold for a garden. When these scraps are piled together in a corner, tiny living things begin to break them down. Over a few weeks the pile rots into a dark, crumbly soil called compost. This compost is full of food that plants love. By composting, we turn waste into healthy soil instead of dumping it away.
payload.title: How composting turns kitchen waste into rich soil
decoys: Vegetable peels can be piled in a corner
Gardens need a lot of care
Compost is full of food that plants love

payload.passage: The thin blanket of air around our planet is more delicate than it seems. It holds the oxygen we breathe and traps just enough warmth to keep us cosy. It also shields us from the sun's harsher rays. When smoke and waste gases pour into it, this blanket grows unhealthy and the climate begins to shift. Keeping the air clean protects the very thing that lets us live.
payload.title: Why our planet's thin layer of air must be kept clean
decoys: The air holds the oxygen we breathe
The earth is a special place
Waste gases make the air unhealthy

payload.passage: A pinch of care for the soil rewards a gardener for years. Soil that is fed with compost and old leaves grows dark and crumbly. Worms and tiny living things thrive within it and keep it loose. Such living soil holds water well and feeds the plants steadily. Looking after the soil first is the surest way to a thriving garden.
payload.title: Why caring for the soil makes a garden thrive
decoys: Compost makes the soil dark and crumbly

payload.passage: Have you wondered why your shadow grows long in the evening but short at noon? A shadow appears wherever your body blocks the sun's light.
